title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
This incident centers on the use of copyrighted music to train an AI music generation system without authorization from rights holders. The AI system learned to produce original-sounding music from text prompts, and the allegation is that this capability was built by ingesting existing recordings without licenses. The failure occurred at the data-collection and model-training stage, before any output was generated for users, meaning the legal exposure was baked in from the start of development.

The settlement between Udio and Universal Music Group, and separately Warner Music Group, resolved some claims and produced licensing agreements for a future platform restricted to authorized material. Sony Music filed a separate, subsequent lawsuit alleging that over 30,000 recordings were used to train the models, and a class action by independent artists was also allowed to proceed, transferred from Illinois to New York rather than dismissed. The breadth of claimed infringement, spanning multiple major labels and independent artists, points to a systematic absence of rights-clearance review during training data curation.

What is not established is that any court has issued a final finding of infringement, that the training data did in fact contain the specific recordings alleged, or that any intent to infringe has been proven. Lawsuits and settlements are not verdicts.

summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, which had been accused of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system. The dispute centered on Udio's ability to generate original music from text prompts, allegedly by learning from existing hits without permission. Under the settlement, Udio has agreed to launch a new platform next year that will only use authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs while compensating artists involved.

The agreement marks Udio's first licensing deal with a major music label and reflects ongoing tensions between the entertainment industry and AI companies. UMG, along with Sony Music and Warner Music Group, had originally sued Udio for creating songs with similar melodies and chords to popular tracks like The Temptations' "My Girl." Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by investors including will.i.am, has already accumulated millions of users since launching. The settlement's financial terms were not disclosed by either party.
